message.content: {"answer": "E", "option_text": "Hypersensitivity pneumonitis", "reason": "The chest X-ray shows bilateral, ill-defined nodular opacities predominantly in the upper and mid-lung zones (highlighted by yellow circles), with sparing of the costophrenic angles. The classifier returned no strong findings (>0.8) and the report generator described 'clear lungs', which contradicts the visible parenchymal abnormalities; per skill t000003, visual evidence of diffuse/nodular opacity overrides the negative tool output. This pattern of centrilobular nodules/ground-glass opacities in the upper/mid zones is characteristic of Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis, distinguishing it from the lobar consolidation of CAP (A), the dependent edema of chemical pneumonitis (B), or the migratory/peripheral opacities of organizing pneumonia (D)."}
